summary.title: Setting up
summary.one_liner: You learn how to set up the basic framework for a 2D OpenGL game (Breakout): a Game class with init/input/update/render, shader and texture utility classes, and a resource manager singleton.
takeaways: Structure a 2D game around a Game class with Init, ProcessInput, Update and Render functions.
Use a GameState enum (active, menu, win) to vary processing and rendering by state.
Wrap shaders and textures in reusable classes, and load resources through a static resource manager singleton.
Enable blending and skip depth testing for an entirely 2D scene to avoid z-fighting.
summary.summary: This page is the first part of the LearnOpenGL Breakout 2D game series and sets up the project framework. It defines a Game class with state, input key array, resolution, and init/process-input/update/render functions, plus a GameState enum. It then introduces utility Shader and Texture classes and a static ResourceManager for loading resources, and covers the GLFW window setup with blending enabled and depth testing disabled. Full code listings are linked from the page rather than shown in the text.
